summary: Sodium hyaluronate is the sodium salt of hyaluronic acid, a naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan used as a topical skin hydrator/protectant, ocular lubricant, viscosupplement for joints, and surgical viscoelastic. It acts locally by retaining water and providing lubrication; systemic effects are negligible.
indications: Topical skin moisturizer, conditioner and skin protectant (cosmetic / dermatologic use)
Ocular lubrication for dry eye (ophthalmic formulations)

dosage.d: Apply to clean skin per product directions
1-2 drops in affected eye(s) as needed

admin: Start with clean hands and clean skin for topical application
Do not use applicators if the sterile seal is broken
For topical serum, apply with even strokes and allow absorption
Ophthalmic drops: avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or surfaces
Intra-articular and surgical uses are administered by trained clinicians under aseptic technique
moa: Sodium hyaluronate is a high-molecular-weight glycosaminoglycan that binds large amounts of water, producing viscous, viscoelastic and lubricating properties. Topically it hydrates and forms a protective film on skin; in the eye it stabilizes the tear film; in joints it restores the viscoelasticity of synovial fluid, lubricating and cushioning the joint.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to hyaluronate or formulation components
Active infection at the application or injection site
relative: Broken skin barrier or open wounds (topical) unless directed
Avian protein allergy for certain avian-derived products
monitor: Signs of infection at injection sites

preg: Topical and ocular use involves negligible systemic absorption and is generally considered low risk. Use intra-articular preparations only if clearly needed and after clinician assessment.
lact: Topical and ocular use is considered compatible with breastfeeding given minimal systemic exposure.
renal: No dose adjustment required; locally administered with negligible systemic absorption.
hepatic: No dose adjustment required; locally administered with negligible systemic absorption.

minor: Concurrent topical irritants may increase local irritation
interactions.diagnostics: No known interference with laboratory tests.

emergency: Septic arthritis after injection (fever, severe joint pain, swelling)

monitoring: Local skin tolerance and absence of irritation
Ocular comfort and any persistent redness/pain
Injection-site for signs of infection or inflammatory flare
counsel: Apply only to clean, intact skin unless otherwise directed
Stop use and consult a clinician if irritation persists
For eye drops, avoid contaminating the dropper tip
Report fever or severe joint pain after intra-articular injection
Do not use if packaging seal is broken
pk: Local; degraded by hyaluronidase (hours to days in tissue)
Hours to days depending on formulation
Store per product label; protect from freezing
pearls: Naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan; acts locally with negligible systemic absorption
High water-binding capacity underlies its hydrating and viscoelastic effects
Cross-linked dermal/intra-articular forms last longer than free solution
Maintain aseptic technique for ocular and intra-articular use
missed: For scheduled topical or ophthalmic use, apply when remembered and resume the usual routine; no need to double up. Intra-articular series should follow the clinician's schedule.
overdose: Overdose is not clinically relevant for topical/ocular use given negligible systemic absorption. Excess local application may cause transient irritation; manage with gentle cleansing and discontinuation.
